title: Invertibility of the canonical divisor section on the complement
statement: Let i:D -> T be any closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and W the complement of its image. The canonical divisor section pulled back to W, defined by [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] as a map from the pulled-back unit module to the pulled-back dual of the ideal sheaf, is an isomorphism. In particular, when the ideal is invertible, it defines its prescribed complementary frame.

source.place: (G1), inverse local equations and the canonical complementary section

proof.text: The support of the ideal of a closed immersion is its closed image. On the complementary open its ideal inclusion into the unit module is an isomorphism. The explicit canonical divisor section is the dual of this inclusion composed with the unit internal-Hom isomorphism; this equality follows on sections by commutativity of multiplication.

source.place: (G1), inverse local equations and the canonical complementary section

proof.text: Open restriction commutes with internal Hom. Its naturality square identifies restriction of the dual inclusion, followed by that comparison, with the internal-Hom map induced by the restricted ideal inclusion. The latter is an isomorphism, so the restricted dual inclusion and canonical divisor section are isomorphisms.

source.place: (G1), inverse local equations and the canonical complementary section

proof.text: Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the specified tensor-pullback section with ordinary pullback of the divisor section. The restriction-versus-pullback isomorphism transports the preceding invertibility. This also covers the empty complementary open.
